clue.text: Man's seldom indisposed, eating fine prepared fish

indicators.note: eating means the shuffled letters take another piece inside them
indisposed means out of sorts, so the letters of these words are put out of order

parts.note: OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A man who is rarely unwell has fallen ill after eating some fancy prepared fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indisposed' reads as illness but signals the shuffle into SMEDSALMON; 'eating' sets the word for fine inside it. 'prepared' belongs with 'fish' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoking is a way of curing and preparing salmon, a fish served as a delicacy.

clue.text: Fluttering bluetits, feature of foreign film?

indicators.note: fluttering suggests birds flapping about, so the letters of the bird name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Blue tits flapping about appear, perhaps, as a scene in some arty foreign film.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign films are commonly shown with translated captions at the bottom of the screen, so these captions are a typical feature.

clue.text: Yours truly and heads of section happily work together

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way for a speaker to say me

indicators.note: heads of means the first letters of the words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: A manager says that they and the leaders of a department cooperate cheerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when their teeth engage, so the word means fit or cooperate well with one another.

clue.text: One consuming much alcohol and cake

definitions.meaning: a heavy drinker who soaks up drink like an absorbent pad
a light airy cake such as a Victoria sandwich

explanation.definitionFit: Both a soak who drinks heavily and a light airy cake share this name, from the absorbent sea creature.

clue.text: Half of soap boxes used by this Athenian philosopher

indicators.note: half of means only the first two of the four letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: crates are wooden boxes for goods

explanation.surface: An Athenian thinker is said to have used half a bar of soap and some boxes, perhaps as a soapbox.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to soapbox oratory; 'used by this' just ties the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the classical Greek thinker of Athens, teacher of Plato, put to death in 399 BC.

clue.text: Not fully prepared to study

indicators.note: not fully means the word is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: ready means prepared

explanation.surface: Someone not quite ready is told to go and revise.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is to study it, especially at a university.

clue.text: Computer accessory needed by famous engineer

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A well-known engineer needs a gadget for the PC.
explanation.definitionFit: A handheld pointing device is a standard accessory plugged into a computer.

clue.text: Potter's unorthodox demonstration

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A potter's unusual display of work at an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstration' reads as a craft display, but it means a public rally of dissent.
explanation.definitionFit: A public march or rally expressing objection is a demonstration.

clue.text: Road, though far from smooth, will lead to Far East

parts.note: tho is an informal short spelling of though
rough is the opposite of smooth
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A bumpy road will take you to the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far East' looks like one place, but splits into FAR and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or public street through a place is a thoroughfare.

clue.text: Kenneth longing to go inside part of house

indicators.note: to go inside means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Ken is the short form of the name Kenneth
an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: Kenneth is eager to enter a room of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where food is cooked is one part of a house.

clue.text: Sat astride horse, nothing more, in Wild West show

parts.note: to sit astride a horse and travel is to ride, past tense rode
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cowboy rode a horse and did nothing else at a frontier show.
explanation.definitionFit: An American cowboy contest of bronco riding and roping is a classic Wild West entertainment.

clue.text: Discourage fellow cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
a gent is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man to put off the cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' looks like a person, but it is a washing product.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a chemical cleaning agent such as washing powder.

clue.text: After religious lessons, judged free of sin?

indicators.note: after puts the word for judged after the lessons piece in the answer

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
deemed means judged or considered

explanation.surface: After Bible classes, someone was considered cleansed of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a school subject in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian theology one saved and delivered from sin is described this way; the question mark flags the looser phrasing.

clue.text: Supporting member of rugby team, for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means most of the word is used, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: A fan backs one rugby player most of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: A prop is a front-row forward in a rugby scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pro something is to be in favour of it, backing it.

clue.text: Convicted criminal lying about sources of illegal stash, right?

indicators.note: about means the lying word goes around the other letters

parts.note: prone means lying face down

indicators.note: sources of means the first letters of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: Is a convict fibbing about where his hidden haul came from?
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' suggests telling lies; here it means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone convicted and jailed is held as an inmate in custody.

clue.text: Had meal in canteen regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone routinely had lunch in the works dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To have eaten is the past tense of eat, so having a meal is this.

clue.text: Loathing of French examination process

parts.note: de is French for of
testing is the process of examining

explanation.surface: A student hates the French exam procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe intensely, so the present participle means loathing.

clue.text: Teachers sound disapproving or start to shout

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Teachers either cluck in disapproval or begin to yell.
explanation.definitionFit: Private teachers who coach individuals or small groups are tutors.

clue.text: Minister's house fellow swore is empty

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: is empty means the inside letters go, leaving only the first and last

explanation.surface: A man cursed at the vicarage when he found it deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: A manse is chiefly the Scottish Presbyterian minister's house.
explanation.definitionFit: The official residence of a Presbyterian or other Protestant minister is called a manse.

clue.text: Creature wife caught in trap

indicators.note: caught in means the letter goes inside the trapping word

parts.note: a net is a trap for catching

explanation.surface: An animal was netted along with someone's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amphibian like a salamander is one example of a creature.

clue.text: Satirise cake-making competition, with different introduction

indicators.note: with different introduction means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a bake-off is a baking contest, as in TV's The Great British Bake Off

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a TV baking contest by giving it a new opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great British Bake Off is a popular UK TV baking contest; its B becomes T.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a take-off is to mimic or parody, so the phrasal verb means satirise.

clue.text: Feature of soccer game, something thrilling

definitions.meaning: striking the ball with the foot is central to football
a thrill or buzz, as in doing something for fun

explanation.definitionFit: Footballers strike the ball with the foot, and a thrill or buzz is the same word in slang.

clue.text: When it's Hogmanay, we yearn to go wild

indicators.note: to go wild means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: At the Scottish winter festival we long to party wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish celebration of 31 December.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish festival on the last night of December, the eve of the coming calendar year.

clue.text: Some letters from article are easily understood

indicators.note: Some letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Parts of a written piece can be grasped readily.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and lucid writing is easy to follow, which is what this means.
